policy: Existing source/explicit ALL or ANY / existing joined candidate / matching original request; lexicographic request ID then candidate ID. No use-label, known result or ease criterion. Selected once before calibration; no replacement.

request.predicate: Neither continued jointness nor complete separation of the remaining coparceners is presumed merely from the admitted separation and partitioned share of one member; their status requires independent factual examination.
request.model_limited_conclusion: At the Supreme Court civil appellate stage, the decisive finding was that Ram Narain and his nephew Ram Saran had separated during Sheo Narain's lifetime and remained separate when Ram Narain died in 1926. The Court reached that finding principally through Exhibits 2, 2(a) and 2(b), admitted and weighed in context, rather than through any presumption or the plaintiff's bare assertion. The defendants' account that only Imrit separated was rejected after examination of the contrary documents and later joint dealings. Ram Saran consequently did not inherit Ram Narain's property by Mitakshara survivorship. The judgment recognized succession through Sumitra to Ramsawari but did not thereby establish that the plaintiff could recover every property or the entirety of every jointly acquired asset.

request.predicate: The extent of Ganeshi Lal's subrogation against his co-mortgagors was determined by the equitable principles adopted in the judgment, not by directly applying sections 92 or 95 or the previous sections 74 and 75 of the Transfer of Property Act.
request.model_limited_conclusion: The Supreme Court conclusively rejected Ganeshi Lal's assignment theory, full-face-debt contribution theory and procedural objection as presented, and affirmed the equitable actual-expenditure limitation applicable to the redeemed joint mortgage. Its disposition did not extinguish the other co-sharers' rights, eliminate Ganeshi Lal's recognized right to equitable contribution, fix the plaintiffs' ultimate shares, determine Punjab customary succession questions or settle the statutory operation of section 92. Those limitations are essential to the scope of the judgment.
